content: Server actions vs route handlers: use smallest server boundary matching the caller. Server Actions = private app mutations from own UI (forms, dialogs), support revalidatePath/redirect, no URL contract. Route Handlers = real HTTP endpoints for external clients, webhooks, custom responses/status codes, file serving, cacheable GET data. Neither should own business logic — extract shared rules into a lib/services layer (typed server-only functions) that both entry points delegate to. Route handler = transport: parse request, verify auth, call service, map to response. Action = entry point: parse input, check user, call service, revalidate. Anti-pattern: duplicating the same rule in an action and a handler (drifts). Service function keeps transport swappable.
